$comment: THE SANCTIONED BREAKPOINT LADDER — the single source of truth for every
Why this file exists: a CSS custom property cannot appear in a media query
prelude, so the literal rem values must be repeated at every call site.
That repetition is unavoidable; going UNCHECKED is not. Before WUFPA-080,
15 media-query blocks duplicated four thresholds against five documented in
docs/07 section 5.1, and one value in active use (40rem) appeared in neither
list. Nothing caught it because nothing was looking.
scripts/check-framework.mjs (WUFPA-084, guard #3) reads this file and fails
the build on any @media threshold not listed in `sanctioned` or
docs/07 section 5.1 in step — changing one without the others is exactly the
drift this file exists to stop.

sanctioned.what: Two-column layouts; footer 2x2; gutter steps to --space-6
Desktop nav; three-up grids; sidebars; gutter steps to --space-8

transitional.why: All three are card grids going one-up to two-up. They should not be media queries at all — the intrinsic `.grid` primitive in global.css (repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...))) already does this by available space rather than viewport, which is what docs/21 section 12 means by 'recompose, don't resize'. Left in place deliberately: refactoring them belongs to WUFPA-015 (with the page-level ones owned by WUFPA-050 and WUFPA-052), not to WUFPA-080, and silently rewriting three components under a token task would blur exactly the boundaries this queue keeps sharp.

notes.unusedButSanctioned: --bp-xl and --bp-2xl currently have no call sites. That is fine and is NOT drift: the ladder is a sanctioned vocabulary, not a usage record. The guard errors on unsanctioned values, never on unused sanctioned ones.
notes.maxWidthQueries: docs/07 section 5.1 states mobile-first, min-width only. Two max-width queries exist (Breadcrumb.astro truncation, Button.astro block-at-small) — both are genuine narrow-viewport exceptions rather than a desktop-first layout, and both use sanctioned values.
